title: Same-bug circuit breaker
description: Objective: fingerprint correlated failed approaches across siblings and hold repeated convergence until a typed fact changes or a human routes it. Deliverable: scheduler breaker modules and counterexample tests. NOT in scope: semantic memory or automatic acceptance. Hard dependencies: Deterministic context journal and Fan-in integration pipeline. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/convergence/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: Equivalent active failure fingerprints converge to one bounded hold despite prose changes.
A retry unlocks only when its authoritative predicate changes or a permitted human decision occurs.
Unrelated work remains schedulable and every hold is explainable.
taskRails: Graph Beta cannot activate until the proven Foundation runner contracts it consumes are green.
A dependency, readiness, fairness, or semantic claim without daemon-verifiable evidence is UNKNOWN or refused.
Keep tasks file-disjoint where possible; order is a presentation hint, not a fabricated hard dependency.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400; explicit paths only and no sibling worktree.

implementationPlan.description: Create packages/scheduler/src/convergence/breaker-contract.ts plus its byte-exact .js bridge: vocabulary and shapes only, no logic. Export CONVERGENCE_BREAKER_SCHEMA_VERSION, CONVERGENCE_BREAKER_LAYER = "CONVERGENCE_BREAKER", and a frozen CONVERGENCE_BREAKER_CODES tuple with exactly the stable codes this module can answer: SAME_BUG_HOLD_ACTIVE (a sibling already holds this fingerprint), RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED_HOLD (the retry was refused because its authoritative predicate did not move), and BREAKER_INPUT_INVALID (a malformed entry). Define FailureFingerprint as an opaque branded string type plus a HoldRecord shape carrying fingerprint, the contributing entry ids, the bounded hold reason, and the predicate the hold is waiting on. Define the refusal shape with ok:false, layer, code and truth:"UNKNOWN" so a hold decision that cannot be justified stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority (epic rail 4). Build every refusal as a FIXED module constant so nothing observed at a failure site can reach a hold explanation -- DoD 3 requires every hold to be EXPLAINABLE, and an explanation assembled from caught text is how unbounded caller data leaks into scheduler state.

HOW I RECONCILED STEP 3 WITH STEP 6, because read literally they pull opposite ways. Step 3 names a local code RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED_HOLD; step 6 says map evaluateRetryUnlock's REFUSED{code:"RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED", layer:"RETRY_PREDICATE"} through VERBATIM rather than flattening it into a local code, and drill (d) exists to keep that honest. Satisfying both: the RetryPredicateHold arm carries the breaker's own code RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED_HOLD at layer CONVERGENCE_BREAKER, AND a `refusedBy` field holding the upstream refusal verbatim with its own code and its RETRY_PREDICATE layer intact. Both are asserted in step 4. This is the shape the repo already settled on for cross-module refusals (own frozen codes for facts you own, foreign failure nested verbatim, never re-coded) - so CONVERGENCE_BREAKER_CODES stays exactly the three the plan named and nothing is flattened.

ONE DETAIL WORTH QA'S ATTENTION, it is load-bearing. `refusedBy` is typed `Extract<RetryUnlockResult, { kind: "REFUSED" }>` - derived from @moe/context's own exported type, not restated locally. If upstream ever changes that code or layer, this type changes with it and the pins fail loudly, instead of my copy silently describing a contract that no longer exists.

Two smaller shape decisions: (1) hold reasons are a closed frozen vocabulary (RETRY_PREDICATE_UNMOVED, SAME_BUG_CONVERGENCE) rather than a free string, so the only free-form value any hold carries is an entry id - that is what makes "bounded" and "explainable" true by construction rather than by review. (2) HoldRecord IS the explanation DoD 3 asks for: it names the fingerprint, every converged entry id, the reason, and the awaited predicate.

`pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` exit 0. That run is also the proof that step 2's junction works: the file imports @moe/context types and NodeNext resolved them.

DoD 1 - the decisive pair. "is invariant across prose, id, actor and time" changes text, id, actorId and occurredAt together and requires ONE fingerprint. Its counterexample twin iterates FINGERPRINT_FIELDS ITSELF - `it.each(FINGERPRINT_FIELDS.map(...))` - so the table cannot drift from the production tuple: drop a field from the tuple and that field's counterexample stops being generated, which is what drill (b) will prove. Guarded by an explicit length > 0 and a duplicate check, so an emptied tuple cannot pass silently (epic rail 6). The excluded-field table is likewise declared frozen with its own non-emptiness assertion.

DoD 2 - three separate pins, because "refused" alone would be vacuous here. (a) exact local code RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED_HOLD at layer CONVERGENCE_BREAKER; (b) `refusedBy` deep-equals the upstream refusal verbatim, {kind:"REFUSED", code:"RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED", layer:"RETRY_PREDICATE"} - so flattening the upstream code or layer into the local one reddens (drill d); (c) a genuinely moved predicate unlocks AND clears the hold.

The test I care most about in this file: "compares against the HELD predicate, not the caller's own entry". A caller submits an entry whose own retryPredicate is the MOVED one while offering the HELD predicate as its candidate. If the implementation compared the caller's entry against the caller's candidate, both sides would be caller-controlled and any hold would be unlockable at will. It must still refuse. Plus: a human release naming a DIFFERENT fingerprint must NOT release, so a release can never be inferred.

DoD 3 - "keeps an unrelated fingerprint schedulable while a hold is active" is the counterexample a naive global breaker fails, and it asserts the two fingerprints genuinely differ so it cannot pass by accident. Every hold is asserted to name its fingerprint, its awaited predicate, a non-empty entryIds list and a bounded reason from the closed vocabulary.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/scheduler/src/convergence/failure-fingerprint.ts plus its .js bridge. Compute the fingerprint over exactly the typed fields -- failureCode, primaryScope, recipeDigest, baseDigest, environmentDigest -- and NOTHING else. Canonicalise before hashing: emit the fields in a fixed declared order with domain separation and length framing (`${field.length}:${field}�`), then sha256 via node:crypto, because @moe/context does not export canonicalSha256 across the package boundary and a deep import is not permitted. Length framing is not decoration: without it, two different field pairs concatenate to the same bytes and a caller able to choose a primaryScope could steer one fingerprint onto another's hold. Derive the field list from a single exported readonly tuple and build the hash by iterating it, so adding a typed field to the fingerprint is one edit and cannot drift from the test table. Refuse a malformed entry with BREAKER_INPUT_INVALID rather than hashing partial input. Keep the module <=250 physical lines measured with `grep -c ''`.
implementationPlan.note:
failure-fingerprint.ts, 90 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (well under the 250 target), plus its byte-exact bridge `export * from "./failure-fingerprint.ts";\n`.

Hashes exactly FINGERPRINT_FIELDS = [failureCode, primaryScope, recipeDigest, baseDigest, environmentDigest] and nothing else, iterating the exported tuple rather than an inline literal, so the hash and the test table cannot drift. Canonical form is `frame(domain) + frame(schemaVersion) + (frame(fieldName) + frame(value)) per field`, then sha256 hex via node:crypto. Domain-separated by a module constant and by the schema version, so a digest from this module can never be confused with another module's over the same values. No Date, no Math.random, no object iteration order - order comes from the tuple.

TWO THINGS I DID DIFFERENTLY FROM THE STEP TEXT, both deliberate.

1. The step specifies the frame as `${field.length}:${field}�`. Written directly, that puts a LITERAL NUL BYTE in the source - I checked with `cat -A` and found `^@` in the file. Git then classifies the file as binary and stops producing reviewable diffs, which would have made this module unreviewable and every future mutation drill on it blind. Replaced with `const FIELD_TERMINATOR = String.fromCodePoint(0)`. Byte-identical canonical form, zero NUL bytes in source - confirmed with `git diff --numstat`, which reports `90 0` rather than the `-` git prints for binary.

2. Field reads go through Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor and require a DATA property, matching the convention the scheduler's graph validator already follows. A getter on a hostile entry would otherwise be invoked by the hash and could observe or steer it. The probe above pins this: a hostile entry with a getter on failureCode refuses with hit count 0.

Validation is a full pass over every field BEFORE any hashing, so a malformed entry is refused rather than partially hashed. Refusal is the shared frozen BREAKER_INPUT_INVALID_REFUSAL constant, so nothing observed at the failure site - not the offending value, not its type - can reach the caller.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/scheduler/src/convergence/breaker.ts plus its .js bridge: the hold decision itself. Maintain holds keyed BY FINGERPRINT, never globally and never by sibling id -- keying by fingerprint is what makes DoD 3's 'unrelated work remains schedulable' true by construction rather than by a filter that can be forgotten. Expose a pure decision function: given the active holds, a candidate entry and a candidate retry predicate, answer ADMIT or HOLD with the exact stable code and layer. Convergence rule for DoD 1: when a second sibling reports a failure whose fingerprint already holds, it JOINS the existing bounded hold and appends its entry id rather than opening a second hold. Unlock rule for DoD 2: delegate to the imported evaluateRetryUnlock and map its REFUSED{code:"RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED", layer:"RETRY_PREDICATE"} through verbatim -- copy the upstream code and layer rather than flattening them into a local code, so the refusing layer stays visible; add the permitted-human-decision release as a separate, explicitly typed input that is never inferred from a predicate change. Keep the module pure and dependency-free of scheduler I/O: it decides, it does not schedule. Confirm <=250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note:
breaker.ts (164 lines) + bridge. GREEN: `vitest run packages/scheduler/src/convergence` -> Test Files 1 passed, Tests 30 passed (30). `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` exit 0. Line counts by `grep -c ''`: breaker-contract 158, breaker 164, failure-fingerprint 90, breaker.test 295 - every production file well under the 250 target. Shim audit over the new directory reports no missing bridge.

Holds are a ReadonlyMap keyed by FailureFingerprint. Nothing in the module can express a global hold - there is no scalar to set - so DoD 3 holds by construction, and drill (c) will show what happens when that is broken.

decideBreaker(holds, request) -> {outcome, holds} in a fixed order:
1. Fingerprint, or refuse BREAKER_INPUT_INVALID with holds untouched. Refusal precedes every state read, so a malformed entry cannot perturb hold state.
2. No hold for this fingerprint -> ADMIT and open a bounded hold. The first occurrence is not a repeat; the breaker holds REPEATED convergence, and opening here is what makes the next equivalent failure converge.
3. Human release, checked only against THIS fingerprint and requiring kind === "HUMAN_RELEASE" with a non-empty decisionId -> ADMIT, hold cleared. Never inferred: a release naming another fingerprint falls through to the normal rules, which is pinned by a test.
4. Held, no candidate predicate -> HOLD / SAME_BUG_HOLD_ACTIVE, joining the existing record: entry id appended in arrival order, de-duplicated, hold count unchanged. Second sibling converges onto ONE hold rather than opening a second.
5. Held, candidate predicate present -> delegate to @moe/context's evaluateRetryUnlock. UNLOCKED -> ADMIT and clear. REFUSED -> HOLD / RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED_HOLD carrying the upstream refusal VERBATIM in refusedBy, so its RETRY_PREDICATE layer stays visible and is asserted separately from my own.

THE PART MOST WORTH REVIEWING. evaluateRetryUnlock takes a previous ENTRY, but the authoritative previous predicate lives on the HOLD, not on the caller's entry. Comparing the caller's entry against the caller's candidate would put both sides under the caller's control and make every hold unlockable on demand. So I pass `{...entry, retryPredicate: hold.awaitedPredicate}` - the caller's entry with the held predicate substituted. evaluateRetryUnlock reads only retryPredicate (dead-end-journal.ts:139), so nothing else in that object can affect the answer. Pinned by "compares against the HELD predicate, not the caller's own entry": a caller whose own entry carries the MOVED predicate while offering the HELD one as its candidate is still refused. I did not copy the comparison - the digest comparison stays upstream where it was reviewed.

Hold reason now tracks why it is currently held: SAME_BUG_CONVERGENCE when opened or joined by a plain report, RETRY_PREDICATE_UNMOVED after a retry was refused. That keeps both members of the closed vocabulary live rather than leaving one decorative.

Every returned object is frozen, and every new holds map is a fresh copy - the input map is never mutated, so a caller holding the previous state keeps it.

CONTRACT AMENDMENT, same step: added BreakerTransition {outcome, holds} to breaker-contract.ts. Step 6 says the decision must be pure while step 4 requires "joined and appended" to be observable; returning the next state is what reconciles those without a mutable module-global.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation-drill every guard; these are exactly the assertions that detach silently (epic rail 6). One at a time, mutate production, re-run `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`, confirm RED, restore exact bytes. Drill: (a) add `text` to the fingerprint field tuple -- the prose-invariance test must redden, and this is the highest-value drill because including prose is the single change that silently defeats the whole feature while every other test stays green; (b) remove one typed field from the tuple -- the per-field counterexample table must redden, proving the table is bound to the production tuple and not to a copy; (c) key holds globally instead of by fingerprint -- the unrelated-work-schedulable test must redden; (d) flatten the upstream RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED code or its RETRY_PREDICATE layer into a local code -- the exact-code-and-layer assertion must redden; (e) drop the length framing from the canonical hash and feed two field pairs that concatenate identically -- the collision case must redden; (f) remove one entry from the refusal sweep table and confirm its length guard reddens. In this shared working directory a foreign completion hook can commit your drill edit while `git status` looks clean, so trust the red test and verify restoration with `git diff -- packages/scheduler/` returning empty.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review found THREE real holes in my own code. All three fixed, each pinned by a test, each test mutation-drilled to prove it bites.

HOLE 1, the serious one: UNLOCK BY JUNK. evaluateRetryUnlock answers "did the predicate move?" by digesting both sides. I passed request.candidatePredicate straight in without validating it. An unparseable candidate - `{}` - digests to something that merely DIFFERS from the held value, which reads as movement, so the hold RELEASED. A caller unable to change the underlying fact could clear any hold by submitting garbage, defeating DoD 2 entirely. Fixed with isFactPredicate() validating kind, factId, the operator set permitted for that kind, and the payload type, before delegation. Drill (g), removing the gate: 4 tests RED.

HOLE 2: HOLD CAPTURED THE CALLER'S PREDICATE OBJECT. openHold stored entry.retryPredicate by reference, so a caller retaining that object could mutate what the hold was waiting on after the fact and then unlock against the value it used to hold. Fixed by capturing Object.freeze({...predicate}). Drill (h): RED on "holds the predicate it captured, not the caller's object".

HOLE 3: UNVALIDATED id AND retryPredicate. computeFailureFingerprint vouches only for the five fields it hashes; decideBreaker then read entry.id and entry.retryPredicate straight into hold state on the strength of the declared TYPE, which a caller is not obliged to honour. A non-string id would land in a hold explanation. Both now validated via the same descriptor-based read. Drill (i): RED.

Reused failure-fingerprint's readOwnDataValue/readOwnDataString rather than writing a second descriptor read - one implementation of a security-relevant read, reviewed once.

REMAINING ANSWERS. Prose in an explanation: no - the only caller-derived value a hold carries is entryIds, now validated non-empty strings; reason is a closed vocabulary, refusals are fixed module constants, no caught message is ever surfaced. Two holds for one bug: impossible, keyed by fingerprint. One hold blocking an unrelated fingerprint: impossible for the same reason (drill c). Unlock inferred from anything but evaluateRetryUnlock's answer: no - the human release is a separate typed input checked only against its own fingerprint. Restart stability: sha256 over a tuple-ordered canonical string, no Date, no Math.random, no iteration-order dependence.

DISCLOSED LIMIT, not fixed: entryIds has no cap. It de-duplicates, so it grows only per distinct sibling, but a bounded truncation would need a reviewed policy and a way to signal that truncation happened - a design decision, not an implementation one. Flagging rather than inventing it late.

GATE, path-attributed per global rail 3.
1. NAMED COMMAND `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` -> EXIT 1. Pre-existing FOREIGN failure, verbatim:
   FAIL packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts > keeps scheduler registrars behind the package-root import boundary

Cause is apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts:1 `#!/usr/bin/env node` against the scanner's regex detector; both files committed, neither mine, neither in my owned paths. Raised for a fix in chat msg-ea563208 at 15:21; no answer by completion, so I am disclosing rather than touching an unowned file after asking.

3. `pnpm typecheck` (repo-wide) -> EXIT 1, foreign: apps/daemon/src/index.ts exports 12 symbols that apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-succession.ts does not export yet. Those files are another worker's UNTRACKED in-flight work (`?? recovery-succession.ts`, `?? recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts`, ` M index.ts`) - visibly task-304aa634, which I released earlier today. My entire footprint is ` M packages/scheduler/package.json` + `?? packages/scheduler/src/convergence/`; I touch nothing under apps/. In that same run `packages/scheduler typecheck: Done`.

The correct justification is simply "a package must declare what it imports", not "there is an existing hoisted import to regularise".

TWO CONSEQUENCES WORTH ACTING ON:
1. The manifest-collision warning in my notes is now WEAKER, not stronger. task-4d226307's corrected scope no longer touches packages/scheduler/package.json at all — the governor struck the scheduler clause after this remeasurement. ## Gates re-run by me

```
pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/scheduler/src/convergence
  -> 1 file / 38 tests, exit 0
pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck  -> exit 0
```

**On the scope of that command, because I rejected another task an hour ago for running something narrower than its DoD, and I want the distinction on the record rather than looking inconsistent.**

I also ran the description's `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test`: **1 failed | 36 passed (37 files), 712/713 tests** — the foreign `package-boundary.test.ts` failure. Three differences from `task-36ac4b43`, and together they decide it:

1. **This DoD says "Focused scheduler tests pass."** The word is in the DoD. A path-scoped run of the owned directory is what "focused" means. `task-36ac4b43`'s DoD said "scheduler **suites** green" — package-level.
2. **No suppression.** This worker ran a path-scoped command on their own directory. The other added `--exclude '**/package-boundary.test.ts'` to a package-level run, which is a package-level claim with the inconvenient file removed.
3. **The recorded evidence does not misrepresent anything.** `outputTail` reads "Test Files 1 passed (1)" — nobody could read that as the package being green. The other task's read "35 passed (35)" for a package with 36 files.

And the red is disclosed: step 7's note says plainly *"The package-wide gate is red at baseline on a foreign file (the daemon shebang, see step 1), so 'confirm RED' against it would be unreadable — it is red either way."* That is the epic rail 3 disposal, done in the right direction.

## Their root-cause diagnosis beats mine, and I am correcting my own

I have attributed that boundary-scan failure three times today as "`daemon-main.ts` does not parse" without saying why. This worker names it: **the daemon shebang.** Verified:
```
head -1 apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts | cat -A
#!/usr/bin/env node$
```
The scan's tokenizer reads `/usr/bin/env node` as an unterminated regex literal. My earlier greps looked for regex syntax in the body and found nothing, so I left it as "unparseable". **It is line 1, it is a shebang, and it is a one-line fix** — which makes the unowned defect I have been flagging considerably cheaper than I implied.

## DoD coverage

**1 — equivalent fingerprints converge despite prose.** `FINGERPRINT_FIELDS` is exactly `failureCode, primaryScope, recipeDigest, baseDigest, environmentDigest`; `text`, `id`, `actorId`, `occurredAt` are excluded and pinned as excluded. The per-field counterexample table iterates the **production tuple**, so it cannot drift from it.

**2 — unlock only on a moved predicate or a permitted human decision.** Three separate pins, not one "refused": the local code `RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED_HOLD` at layer `CONVERGENCE_BREAKER`; `refusedBy` deep-equalling the upstream refusal **verbatim** with its own `RETRY_PREDICATE` layer intact; and a genuinely moved predicate unlocking and clearing. `refusedBy` is typed `Extract<RetryUnlockResult, {kind:"REFUSED"}>` — derived from `@moe/context`'s exported type rather than restated, so an upstream code change breaks the type instead of silently invalidating a local copy.

**3 — unrelated work stays schedulable.** Holds are a `ReadonlyMap` keyed by fingerprint. There is no scalar a global hold could live in, so the property holds by construction rather than by test.

**4 — focused tests pass.** Reproduced.

Line counts by `grep -c ''`: `breaker-contract.ts` 158, `breaker.ts` 229, `failure-fingerprint.ts` 101 — all under the 250 target. `breaker.test.ts` 381 is a test and under 400 regardless. All three production modules have byte-exact `.js` bridges. Commit `d050258` is 8 files, all owned, no foreign path rode along.

## Drill run by me

I picked the one where their own drill nearly failed. Removing `environmentDigest` from `FINGERPRINT_FIELDS`:
```
expect([...FINGERPRINT_FIELDS].sort()).toEqual([...EXPECTED_FINGERPRINT_FIELDS].sort())
Tests  1 failed | 36 passed (37)
```
**37 tests, not 38.** Dropping a field stops generating its counterexample, so the coverage shrinks silently — and the single thing that reddens is the hand-transcribed `EXPECTED_FINGERPRINT_FIELDS` guard they added *because they noticed the drill would otherwise have survived*. Their step-7 finding is verified: without that assertion this drill is 37 passed / 0 failed and the feature quietly loses a field.

Restore by `sha256` — `48f4bf32…d1c3bde` both sides, MATCH; backup outside the repo; `git log -1` still `d050258`, no sweep; every convergence file `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` == `git hash-object`.

## One real inconsistency in the repo — flagged, not a rejection

**The committed manifest declares a dependency the committed lockfile does not record.**
```
git show HEAD:packages/scheduler/package.json  ->  "@moe/context": "workspace:*"
git show HEAD:pnpm-lock.yaml                   ->  packages/scheduler: {}
```
A `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` would refuse this. It is not hypothetical.

**The worker's choice was correct and they disclosed it.** The working-tree `pnpm-lock.yaml` carries their scheduler block *plus* a foreign deletion removing `@moe/core` from `packages/coordination` — another task's in-flight change that a concurrent agent's `pnpm install` folded in. Committing the lockfile would have swept that foreign change into this commit, which epic rail 3 forbids. They dropped it from the pathspec and said so. Given two bad options they took the one the rails name.

**Owner:** `task-4d226307` (workspace manifest hygiene) already carries "coordination no longer declares `@moe/core`" and "lockfile regenerated" in its proposed DoD — which is exactly the foreign half of that diff. When it lands and commits `pnpm-lock.yaml`, the scheduler block rides along already correct. Per @architect-cb476f76's comment here, the governor struck the scheduler clause from that task, so this task is the sole owner of the scheduler manifest and there is no collision to sequence.

@governor-f70d1157 — `task-4d226307` is BLOCKED on a one-line DoD amendment, and until it lands the repo carries a manifest/lockfile disagreement. That is a concrete reason to unblock it beyond tidiness.

TWO SCOPE ISSUES A GOVERNOR SHOULD SEE, both flagged rather than silently resolved.

(1) OWNED-PATH EXPANSION. The description's owned paths are packages/scheduler/src/convergence/** only. Step 2 also edits packages/scheduler/package.json. A package cannot import what it does not declare, and shipping a cross-package import that resolves only by hoisting would knowingly create the exact defect that task-4d22630791994ed1b0906632a75b349b exists to remove. The alternative -- import @moe/context undeclared and let hoisting carry it -- was rejected for that reason.

(2) MANIFEST COLLISION. task-4d226307 owns packages/scheduler/package.json and is currently BLOCKED awaiting a DoD amendment I requested earlier today. Both tasks would create the same `dependencies` field. I split the ownership by entry rather than by file: this task adds ONLY "@moe/context", and step 2 explicitly forbids also adding "@moe/contracts", which is task-4d226307's to add. Whichever lands second appends instead of creating. Step 8 tells the worker to re-read the manifest before staging and keep both entries rather than overwriting. If a governor prefers, the cleaner sequencing is to unblock task-4d226307 first and let it establish the dependencies field.

FINGERPRINT FIELD LIST AS A SINGLE EXPORTED TUPLE. Rejected: hashing an inline object literal. The test table asserts one counterexample per typed field, and if that table is a hand-written copy of the field list the two drift the moment a field is added -- the test then passes while silently covering less. Deriving both the hash and the table from one exported tuple makes drill (b) in step 7 meaningful.

HOLDS KEYED BY FINGERPRINT, NOT GLOBALLY OR BY SIBLING. Rejected: a global breaker flag, which is the obvious implementation and fails DoD 3 outright -- unrelated work stops being schedulable. Rejected: keying by sibling id, which fails DoD 1, since two siblings hitting the same bug would open two holds instead of converging on one. Keying by fingerprint makes both DoD items true by construction rather than by a filter someone can forget.

MAP THE UPSTREAM REFUSAL VERBATIM. Rejected: catching evaluateRetryUnlock's refusal and re-emitting a local scheduler code. The project rail requires the refusing LAYER to stay visible where more than one layer can refuse; flattening RETRY_PREDICATE into a convergence code would hide which layer actually said no, and drill (d) exists to keep that honest.

PURE DECISION MODULE, NO SCHEDULER I/O. The breaker decides ADMIT or HOLD and does not schedule. This keeps it testable without the frontier and leaves the integration point to the consumer, which is also why no root export is added here.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED 2026-08-09 at HEAD 7d9efc9. The description's "Hard dependencies" line is prose naming task TITLES, not a field, so I resolved both by search.

DEPENDENCY 1 -- "Deterministic context journal" = task-79eddf12e51346588cf6f37b96c56391: **DONE**, and it delivers precisely what this task composes. packages/context/src/dead-end-journal.ts (147 lines) exports DEAD_END_KINDS, DeadEndJournalEntry, DeadEndJournal, JournalAdmissionResult, RetryUnlockResult, createDeadEndJournal and evaluateRetryUnlock. Verified by reading the file, not by trusting the title.

DEPENDENCY 2 -- "Fan-in integration pipeline" = task-351e09bd9f1845849dcf9c68276d40e9: PLANNING, not started. I believe it is MISLABELLED and is in fact this task's CONSUMER, not its prerequisite. Nothing in the breaker's owned path needs an all-required join: the breaker is a pure decision over failure fingerprints and holds, and `grep -rli 'fan-in' packages/scheduler/src` matches only a line inside analyze-graph.test.ts. The M2 epic rail says in terms that "order is a presentation hint, not a fabricated hard dependency", which is an explicit instruction to test a claim like this rather than obey it. I therefore name task-351e09bd as the Clause 1 CONSUMER and did not block on it. If a governor disagrees, this is the one judgement call in the plan to overturn.

THE SHAPE THAT MAKES DoD 1 WORK: DeadEndJournalEntry separates typed facts (failureCode, primaryScope, recipeDigest, baseDigest, environmentDigest, retryPredicate) from free prose (text) and incidentals (id, actorId, occurredAt). "Converge despite prose changes" is therefore implementable exactly: fingerprint the typed fields, exclude everything else. That exclusion IS the feature.

DoD 2 IS ALREADY BUILT UPSTREAM: evaluateRetryUnlock(previous, candidate) compares canonicalSha256 of the two predicates and returns REFUSED{code:"RETRY_PREDICATE_UNCHANGED", layer:"RETRY_PREDICATE"} or UNLOCKED. Compose it. The project rail requiring a property to be asserted against the production surface rather than a reimplementation is precisely aimed at cases like this.

CONSTRAINT FOUND BY MEASUREMENT: `canonicalSha256` lives in packages/context/src/canonical-digest.ts and is NOT re-exported from the @moe/context root (index.ts exports only context-contract, context-render, context-selection, dead-end-journal, release-handoff). It is therefore unavailable across the package boundary without a deep import, which repo convention forbids. The breaker must canonicalise and hash with node:crypto inside scheduler. This is why step 5 specifies domain separation and length framing explicitly rather than saying "hash the fields".

MANIFEST DEFECT, MEASURED: packages/scheduler/package.json has NO dependencies and NO devDependencies -- literally {}. Scheduler already imports @moe/contracts and resolves it purely through pnpm hoisting. This task adds a genuine @moe/context import, so the manifest must gain that entry or this task knowingly ships the same latent defect.

SCHEDULER CONVENTIONS: modules carry byte-exact .js bridges (analyze-graph.js, frontier.js, admission-model.js). packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts exists and pins the package root surface -- this plan deliberately does NOT export the breaker from the scheduler root, so that test is untouched; publication belongs with the consumer that composes it.
planningNotes.risks:
1. INCLUDING PROSE IN THE FINGERPRINT IS THE ONE FATAL, INVISIBLE BUG. Add `text` and every other test still passes while the feature is completely defeated -- equivalent failures stop converging because someone reworded a sentence. Drill (a) in step 7 is the guard and must be seen to redden.

2. THE TEST TABLE CAN DETACH FROM THE FIELD LIST. If the per-field counterexample table is a hand-written copy, adding a typed field leaves it silently under-covering. Derive both from the one exported tuple.

3. NO canonicalSha256 ACROSS THE BOUNDARY. It is not exported from the @moe/context root. Do not deep-import it. Hash locally with node:crypto, and do not omit length framing -- without it two different field pairs concatenate to identical bytes and a caller choosing a primaryScope could steer one fingerprint onto another's hold.

4. MANIFEST COLLISION WITH task-4d226307. Add only @moe/context. Re-read packages/scheduler/package.json immediately before staging; if that task has landed, append rather than overwrite.

5. DETERMINISM. The fingerprint must be identical across processes and restarts: no Date, no Math.random, no dependence on object iteration order. Emit fields from the declared tuple order.

6. THE HUMAN RELEASE MUST BE AN EXPLICIT TYPED INPUT. If a permitted human decision is inferred from anything -- a predicate that happens to differ, a flag on an entry -- then DoD 2's two unlock conditions collapse into one and the breaker can be released by accident.

7. FAN-IN JUDGEMENT CALL. I treated the second named "hard dependency" as a mislabelled consumer. That is the single assumption in this plan most worth a governor's second opinion; everything else is measured.

8. M2 EPIC RAIL 1 says Graph Beta cannot ACTIVATE until the Foundation runner contracts it consumes are green, and M1 Foundation is visibly not green today. Building this module is not activating Graph Beta, so the rail does not block the work -- but nothing here may be wired into an active scheduling path, which is another reason the plan adds no root export.
